messages:
julie_support: FYI — customer reported JSON mode streaming failures across Py + Go SDKs after upgrading to our hosted endpoint. They get parse errors mid-stream and app crashes. Customer account: acct-42.

julie_support: attaching the raw stream snippet they captured (they said this comes out of the wire, not modified):
```
{"id":1,"meta":{"user":"alice","note":"line1
par\"t"},"text":"hello"}
{"id":2,"meta":{"user":"bob"},"text":"world"}
```

julie_support: note the first JSON looks split across chunks for them (escape sequence and newline in the meta.note). Python sdk raises json.JSONDecodeError when it tries to json.loads on partial buffer.

ev an_support: can you paste the customer SDK versions + request_id? also do they get the same with curl?

julie_support: SDKs: python v2.3.2, go v1.8.0, ts v0.9.5. Request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Customer says curl --no-buffer against our streaming endpoint returns same chunking.

samir_eng: thanks. please also include the raw bytes (use tcpdump or curl -v > raw.bin) — if there's a chunk-boundary inside an escape or unicode seq that explains decode failures on client parsers.

julie_support: repro code from customer (py):
```py
import requests, json
resp = requests.get('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?json_mode=stream', stream=True)
buf = b''
for chunk in resp.iter_content(16):
    buf += chunk
    try:
        # naive: try to parse whenever we see a newline
        if b'}\n{' in buf:
            parts = buf.split(b'\n')
            for p in parts[:-1]:
                json.loads(p)
            buf = parts[-1]
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        print('JSON error', e)
        raise
```

julie_support: python error: JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 28 (char 27)

kevin_go: in Go they get: json: unexpected end of JSON input (or io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) when using json.Decoder on stream.Decoding one by one.

alice_ts: TS client shows "Unexpected token \" in JSON at position 34" — chunk boundary split inside an escaped quote.

samir_eng: this looks like runtime chunking changed — we recently tweaked kernel-level socket buffer size and the streaming layer's write chunk size during the v2.12.0 rollout. @cheng_runtime can you confirm rolling change?

cheng_runtime: looking. I see a deploy yesterday (2026-03-16) that adjusted stream flush sizes to improve latency for small tokens. deploy-bot posted the rollout: v2.12.0 -> streaming-flush optimized.

deploy-bot: [deploy] runtime/v2.12.0 rolled to prod on 2026-03-16T22:03:12Z (change: streaming flush granularity reduced to 16 bytes, toggles: experimental-chunking).

samir_eng: aha. that matches — smaller flush size can produce splits inside multibyte escapes or user-inserted \n sequences. We'll reproduce locally with the same flags.

ev an_support: customer is hitting production crash, can we offer a short-term workaround?

alice_ts: workaround options: 1) recommend customer set json_mode=ndjson (line-delimited JSON) or set buffering on client side to accumulate until full object close ('}'). 2) ship a tolerant-stream parser in next prerelease that buffers until matching braces and handles split escapes.

kevin_go: quick fix for Go is to use bufio.Reader and implement a readUntilTopLevelObject() that counts braces and ignores in-string braces; less brittle than per-chunk json.Decoder for this fragmentation.

samir_eng: plan: reproduce locally, add integration test that injects chunk boundaries at arbitrary offsets including inside escape sequences, then fix runtime or add safe framing header. I'll open ENG issue and link here. Julie — can you confirm customer will accept temporary ndjson advice while we investigate?

julie_support: confirmed they can try ndjson as immediate mitigation. I'll send steps and ask for raw capture (tcpdump + hexdump) to DM.

samir_eng: opening ENG-ISSUE-5238, will tag eng-runtime and sdk teams. assigning to @cheng_runtime to validate whether toggles should be rolled back or pursue framing header in runtime.

cheng_runtime: will check metrics to see if rollback is necessary; if so we can patch to 32-byte flush.

julie_support: thanks team — I'll update customer and follow up with logs in DM.

samir_eng: bump here once you DM logs; going to start a local repro harness now.
